liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dark Star** (2 reviews): Highlights Dark Star Jam into Spanish Jam and U.S. Blues as a unique, wordless jam; Clarifies this Dark Star has lyrics, unlike the longer instrumental version from 7/25/74 [22][29]
- **Let It Rock (First and Only Time Played)** (1 review): Notes a rare-only time performance of Let It Rock, plus great Cumberland and Black Peter [23]

## The recordings

- **gd1974-06-23.sbd.OBV.30846.shnf** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 44 songs; 208 min; rated 4.12/5 by 8 [1]
- **gd1974-06-23.aud.obv.96890.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 30 songs; 209 min; rated 3.5/5 by 2 [2]. Said about its sound: Audience recording noted as nice with only minor issues; pops and handclaps corrected [2]
- **gd1974-06-23.sbd.sacks.213.shnf**: soundboard; 30 songs; 193 min [3]
- **gd1974-06-23.sbd.matrix-sb21b.chappell.83489.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 27 songs; 208 min; rated 4.39/5 by 28 [4]
- **gd74-06-23.moore.weiner.gdADT.14265.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 27 songs; 208 min; rated 4.21/5 by 14 [10]. Said about its sound: Reviewer prefers this AUD, noting Phil blows up the Star and the Spanish Jam [30]
- **gd74-06-23.sbd.cribbs.16780.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 27 songs; 187 min; rated 4.37/5 by 63 [13]. Said about its sound: Reviewer describes sweet mellow jamming in To Lay Me Down and China Doll; Real intensity noted at the ends of Let It Grow, Dark Star, and Uncle John; Reviewer calls the Spanish Jam the best of all time, with Phil tearing it up [20][22][24][27][28]

## Around the show

- Reviewer notes Keith is glowing in this show, with the whole band shining [24]
- Dick Latvala calls it a top show, noting 7/19 and 8/6 are strong alternatives [19]
- Listener finds performances strained, contrasting them with the musical telepathy of Missoula 5/14/74 [21]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1974-06-23.sbd.OBV.30846.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Remaster of SBD with AUD patches by Owens Brothers [1]
- **gd1974-06-23.aud.obv.96890.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Jerry Moore; transferred by Owen Brothers remaster of Jerry Moore recording; source: AudMC > DAT>CD>DC6>CD [2]. Also: Editing and mastering by The Wizard; light noise filter and equalization applied [2]
- **gd1974-06-23.sbd.sacks.213.shnf**: transferred by Josh Belkin; source: SBD>ReelM>DAT>CassetteM>DAT(3)>Prodif Plus card > Samplitude 2496 > Plextor 820 burner [3]. Also: AUD source broadcast by WHRB-FM in early 1980s; Phil's Tape timestretched to match SBD [3]
- **gd1974-06-23.sbd.matrix-sb21b.chappell.83489.flac16**: transferred by Chris Chappell; source: Sick Bits Vol. 21b - SBD/AUD Matrix of 2 previously circulating sources: SBD (shnid=213) + AUD (shnid=14265) [4]. Also: SBD mastered by Josh Belkin; AUD recorded by Jerry Moore with AKG D-1000E mics; AUD recorded about 15 rows from stage on center axis using Sony 152 deck [4]
- **gd74-06-23.moore.weiner.gdADT.14265.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Jerry Moore; source: Audience Recording: AKG D-1000E [10]
- **gd74-06-23.sbd.cribbs.16780.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [13]. Also: Notes the show is included on the So Many Roads box set; Mentions a nice AUD patchwork by someone for the recording [28][29]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by RareVinyl.com: [Grateful Dead Dave's Picks Volume 34: Jai-Alai Fronton, Miami, Fl 6/23/74 + Dave's Picks 2020 Bonus Disc 2020 US 3-CD se](https://uk.rarevinyl.com/products/grateful-dead-dave-s-picks-volume-34-jai-alai-fronton-miami-fl-6-23-74-plus-dave-s-picks-2020-bonus-disc-us-3-cd-album-triple-set-r2607314-790468) [32]
- Fan art by Jittery White Guy: [Grateful Dead: Dave's Picks 34 (Miami 1974)](https://www.jitterywhiteguymusic.com/2020/05/grateful-dead-daves-picks-34-miami-1974.html) [33]
- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Jai-Alai Fronton - June 23, 1974](https://www.dead.net/show/june-23-1974) [34]
